newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Grains-Wheat futures little help.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Grains-Wheat futures little help.

text.p: Sydney wheat futures proved little inspiration last week, with most-active contracts trading narrowly.
This week is expected to largely mirror last week, with prices trading in a modest range as the market continues to digest upward revisons to crop forecasts.
"We'd be surprised to see prices much above $160.00 (a tonne)," said a grains dealer.
Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd sees an even higher crop of 20.43 million tonnes, up from 19.40 million forecast a month earlier.
Said one grower: "That's a lot of wheat."
At the start of the week, the AWB left unchanged its estimated pool estimate for Standard White at A$195.00 a tonne.
AWB chairman Trevor Flugge sees the estimate remaining unchanged for at least a month as prices stabilise.
Nearby January and March wheat peaked at A$158.00 and A$160.00 a tonne respectively at the Sydney Futures Exchange, which only slightly above the week's lows.
Revised forecasts of the 1996/97 harvest flattened expectations of a price rally in the week, leaving futures to flounder.

Based on good rains and minimal damage to hail-hit crops in northern New South Wales, the Australian Wheat Board lifted its forecast to 20 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 19 million tonnes previously. If correct, it would mark Australia's second largest crop ever.

Meanwhile, Flugge has presented a bullish outlook for Australian exports to China, with shipments forecast to hold unchanged at 2.2 million tonnes despite expectations of a strong domestic crop in China.
The AWB also unveiled plans to construct an A$8 million to A$10 million grains terminal at the port of Fang Cheng in Guangxi province with Transfield Holdings Pty Ltd.
Australian growers also are monitoring crop developments in Canada, where some weather-related dmage is expected and India, which could default on up to 400,000 tonnes of export sales.
Indian exports are under threat due to soaring domestic prices.
